# Steve Makinen's Power Ratings — stated methodology

> **Source class: GUIDE CONTENT.** Every figure is printed in the 2026 VSiN College Football Betting Guide. No outside research and no post-publication updates.

*Steve Makinen's 2026 College Football Power Rating Projections*, pp. 46–47. TTW reference notes paraphrasing the guide; the judgement throughout is Makinen's.

## What goes into the number

- Analysing the returning players and coaches for each team.
- Adjusting for last year's finish and for the current perception of teams.
- Checking that nothing has been assumed outside the window of normalcy for each team's recent history or for conference strength.

Makinen says that last point has become a bigger challenge each passing year, because some teams completely revamp their rosters through the transfer portal.

- Only 52 teams return their starting quarterback from last season, and several of the most prominent teams from a year ago do not — most notably title-game participants Indiana and Miami (FL).
- He counts 33 head-coaching changes and calls that a fairly high number.

## How the number is used

He runs the adjusted power numbers against the complete schedule to project season standings, and prints a projected power-rating line for every game on all 138 team pages. The conference pages carry, for each team, the DraftKings season win total, the 2026 Makinen power rating, home and road field ratings, schedule strength with national rank, and projected overall and conference records.

## Makinen on his own record

He reports his own recent hit rate without varnish: of the five Power Four or Independent teams he projected to win 10-plus games last year, only one made the CFP — though the year before, four of the five made up the four semifinal teams.

## Projections he highlights

- **Ten-win projections.** For 2026 he has seven teams projected at 10-plus wins: Notre Dame (11.2), Texas Tech (10.7), Oregon (10.3), Indiana (10.2), Miami (FL) (10.1), Ohio State (10.0) and Georgia (10.0), and notes Penn State, Texas and BYU could join them.
- **Schedule strength.** After two straight seasons of Florida playing the toughest schedule nationally, Texas takes over for 2026, ahead of Oklahoma, Kentucky, Mississippi State and Arkansas — all SEC teams, mostly because of conference opponents. The first non-SEC team is Michigan at No. 6. The easiest schedule belongs to UMass, unseating Liberty after three years; its opponents average a 26.21 power rating, which he says is like playing a team at Bowling Green's level every week. Buffalo, Sacramento State and Ohio are next, with Jacksonville State the first non-MAC team at No. 5 and Liberty No. 6.
- **Group of Six.** Boise State (9.2), James Madison (9.1), UNLV (9.0), Navy (8.5) and New Mexico (8.5) carry the highest projected win totals among Group of Six teams, though he notes each faces an early test or two.

On North Texas — the biggest drop — he explains that new head coach Neal Brown is taking over virtually a brand-new team, with no starter back from the 2025 group that went 12-2 and scored 45.1 points per game. He calls James Madison and Tulane two other complete rebuilds for new coaches, and identifies Vanderbilt and Iowa State as the worst drops among Power Four programmes.

## Against the market

- **Over the DraftKings win total.** Against the DraftKings season win totals, he projects more wins than the market for Boise State (+1.7), UNLV (+1.5), Arkansas State (+1.3), Miami (OH) (+1.3), Georgia Southern (+1.3), Western Kentucky (+1.2) and Navy (+1.0). He says the Broncos' +1.7 is one of the biggest differences he has ever had in this exercise, that he double- and triple-checked it, that he thinks the oddsmakers are giving a bit too much credit to the strength of the new Pac-12, and that Boise State is the obvious favorite — with the same logic applying to UNLV, who he expects to benefit greatly from Boise leaving the Mountain West.
- **Under the DraftKings win total.** He projects fewer wins than the market for Northern Illinois (-1.1), Georgia State (-1.0), Florida (-0.9), Sam Houston State (-0.8) and Cal (-0.8). He notes Northern Illinois jumps in conference strength moving from the MAC to the Mountain West, and that Florida gets a new head coach in Jon Sumrall, who he says seems to have the enthusiasm meter pegged but perhaps not the roster yet to compete in what looks like a very strong and balanced SEC.

## One stated general principle

He states one general principle outright: he is not a fan of big conference teams making regular coaching changes when it appears some progress is being made, because it usually sets the programme back.

## What the guide does not state

- No formula, weighting or component breakdown is given. The guide describes the inputs in prose and does not publish how they combine.
- No standard deviation, scale definition or explicit statement that one rating point equals one point of spread appears on pp. 46-47. That relationship is demonstrated separately in the line-model verification, which is TTW-derived arithmetic over the guide's own printed numbers.
- No uncertainty interval, confidence figure or error bar accompanies any rating.
